memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Abraham called that place The Lord Will Provide. And to this day it is said, "On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided." - Gen 22:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham names the place with a name that would echo through the ages: "The Lord Will Provide" - in Hebrew, Yahweh Yireh, "the Lord will see to it." On the mountain where he had faced the loss of everything, Abraham discovered afresh that God provides. And he wanted that truth marked forever in the name of the place.

Notice the tense - "The Lord will provide." Not merely "the Lord provided," past tense, though He certainly had. Abraham looks forward. He senses that this mountain, this principle, this promise of divine provision points to something still to come. And how right he was.

For this was Moriah - the very region where, generations later, Jerusalem would stand, and where, on a hill nearby, God would provide the ultimate sacrifice. What was foreshadowed on this mountain with a ram would be fulfilled on another hill with the Lamb of God. "On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided" - and it was, at Calvary.

This name is a gift to every believer facing an impossible situation. When you cannot see how, when the need is beyond you, when everything seems lost - remember the name of the mountain: The Lord Will Provide. He provided a ram for Abraham. He provided His Son for the world. And He will provide for you, too, "according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus" (Phil 4:19). Trust the God whose very name is Provider.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you facing an impossible situation where you need God to provide?
- How does God's provision at the cross assure you He will provide for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are Yahweh Yireh, the God who provides. You gave a ram for Abraham and Your own Son for me. When I face the impossible, help me trust the God whose very name is Provider. You will provide.
Amen.
